title: Rabbah bar Mari
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman suggests that apparently he was a native of the Land of Israel, and possibly he still merited to see Rabbi Yochanan, as in [Moed Katan 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28b.20-21) and [Sanhedrin 101a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.101a.10), where he said, “Thus said Rabbi Yochanan.”
Likewise, Rabbah bar Mari transmits in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name in [Berakhot 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.42b.3-4) and 44a.
In [Yoma 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.78a.9-10) he relates: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi had a scarf,” etc.

In an alternative attribution at [Sukkah 32b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.32b.2), he teaches in the name of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: “There are two date palms in the Valley of Ben Hinnom,” etc.

Hyman likewise states that we always find the phrase “They say in the West in the name of Rabbah bar Mari,” as in [Yoma 86b:5-6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.86b.5-6), [Sanhedrin 100a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.100a.15-16) and [Zevachim 90b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.90b.6).
Hyman places his descent to Babylonia afterward, as in [Yoma 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.78a.9-10): “When Rabbah bar Mari came,” etc.
Rava received much from him, as in [Moed Katan 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.28b.20-21), where Rava asked him: “It is written of Zedekiah, ‘You shall die in peace,’” etc.

Hyman has Rava ask him in [Yevamot 62b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.62b.6): “From where is this matter that the Rabbis said, that grandchildren are like children?” There, at 63b, he asked him: “It is written,” etc. In [Bava Kamma 92a:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.92a.17), [Bava Kamma 92b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.92b.5) and [Bava Kamma 93a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.93a.2) Rava asked him, “From where is this thing that people say?” and he answered him with a source from a verse, or from a mishnah or baraita.[^4]

Likewise in [Sanhedrin 103b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.103b.13) Rava asked him why they did not count Jehoiakim. There, at [Sanhedrin 101a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.101a.10), Rabbi Abba asked him: “It is written, ‘All the sickness’…” — he said to him, “Thus said Rabbi Yochanan.”

When Rav Dimi came to Babylonia he brought his homilies, in [Sanhedrin 100a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.100a.15-16), where Rav Dimi said to Abaye: “Thus they say in the West in the name of Rava bar Mari: The Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to give each and every righteous person three hundred and ten worlds, as it is said.”
In [Eruvin 86a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.86a.2) Rava bar Mari expounded: “He shall sit forever,” etc.
Hyman classifies all of these as in aggadah, except [Zevachim 90b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.90b.6), where he said: “The sin-offering of idolatry lacks an aleph; it is written lechatat.”[^3]

notes.text: ש״י is310; the defective חטאת spelling lacks aleph. Rabbah/Rava variants within the supplied notice remain visible. The Palestinian origin, possible encounter with Yochanan and classification of nearly all statements as aggadah are Hyman’s observations, not harmonized identities.

In the consulted Sanhedrin 100a the preceding paragraph names Dimi and Abaye; the continuation cites Rava bar Mari and 310 worlds. The supplied Rabbah/Rava forms remain visible. Hyman’s always formula, possible Palestinian origin and encounter with Yochanan, migration and aggadah classification are retained as his conclusions. The defective aleph observation remains as supplied, not an independently inspected printing history.

Berakhot gives Rabbah bar Mari’s transmission in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name. Sanhedrin gives Rav Dimi’s discussion with Abaye and a Western teaching in the name of Rava bar Mari. The name forms retain their local spellings. Heilprin’s parallel notice lists both. See [Heilprin’s parallel notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3170&lang=en).

The consulted Yevamot passage has Rabbah put the question to Rava bar Mari. In the proverbs at Bava Kamma the consulted wording has Rava put his questions to Rabbah bar Mari. Yoma has Rabbah in the Western attribution. Zevachim has Rava in the parallel formula and gives the spelling of “sin-offering” without an aleph.
